How to Resume an OpenCode Session

From the project directory, run opencode --continue to reopen the latest session. For an older conversation, run opencode session list and open the exact ID with opencode --session SESSION_ID. Confirm the earlier messages before sending a new prompt. In OpenCode 2, an ID missing from the current store can create an empty session.

  1. Continue the last session
  2. Find and open a specific ID
  3. Diagnose an empty or missing session
  4. Export and import a session
  5. See the OpenCode 2.4.1 test

Which session do you want to resume?

ContinueSelect by IDCheck project

Continue the last OpenCode session

Open the directory where you started the earlier conversation. Use --continue or its short form -c. In the terminal interface, you can also run /sessions to choose a conversation.

opencode --continue

Check the transcript and directory before you submit a prompt. In scripts, the same option is available on opencode run. This command immediately sends the new prompt, so use it when you know the latest session is the one you want.

opencode run --continue "Summarize the decisions already made."

Find the exact session ID

From the original project directory, list sessions and copy the full ID, including its ses_ prefix. Replace SESSION_ID with that value.

opencode session list --max-count 20 --format json
opencode --session SESSION_ID

Check the directory and title in the list. If you need a script to continue that ID, use opencode run --session SESSION_ID "Your next prompt". In OpenCode 2.4.1 the flag can create a new empty session when the ID is absent. Verify the transcript or list entry before relying on the ID.

Why an OpenCode session may be missing or empty

  1. Verify the directory, including the checkout or worktree where you started the session. A repository with a different initial commit can have a separate project identity. Check the directory in the JSON list instead of relying on its title or ordering alone.
  2. Check the server and user profile. If you previously used a remote server or a container, reconnect to that same server or environment. A private server started with --standalone uses the profile available to that command. Run opencode debug paths to inspect local paths.
  3. If the session is listed but opens without earlier messages, try the original context before sending any data. An empty conversation with the expected ID can be newly created. If you have an export, recover it in the intended project first.

In our two empty Git repositories sharing one temporary profile, session list in one directory displayed the other directory’s session. Running --continue in the second directory started a new conversation. Treat the listed directory and transcript as the confirmation.

For a mismatch between a CLI and a separate service, also check the OpenCode config sources.

Export and import an OpenCode session

Export from the source project and keep the JSON private if you need it for restoration. It can contain prompts, file data or tool output. Then go to the destination directory and import the file there. Use a fresh destination profile to test the import before relying on it.

opencode session export SESSION_ID > session.json
opencode session import /path/to/session.json --directory /path/to/project
opencode session list --format json

Use the ID shown after import. Confirm the earlier messages in the destination before continuing. Restore any uncommitted files separately if the session refers to them.

For sharing, opencode session export --sanitize SESSION_ID removes sensitive transcript and file data as described by OpenCode. Inspect the result before sharing. Keep an original private copy when you need the prior prompts for recovery.

What carried over in OpenCode 2.4.1

ActionHistory sent on the next prompt
--continue after two sessionsMessages from the second session
--session with the first IDMessages from the first session
Export and import into a fresh profileThe first session’s earlier prompts under the original ID
Continue from another empty Git repositoryOnly the new prompt under a new ID
Use an absent ID in a fresh profileOnly the new prompt under the requested ID

We ran the macOS arm64 CLI with isolated projects and a loopback-only provider fixture. The fixture recorded synthetic markers from real requests and returned fixed text. The export retained the tested prompt markers. They were absent from a sanitized export. These observations cover saved history and session selection, without testing model answers or cross-version migration.
